sentences.text: 3 Nancy, Lily and Mitchell!
are meeting to discuss some of the performers who have applied to perform at the concert.
Listen to the meeting and fill in the missing information in the spaces below.
You now have 30 seconds to study the task.
At the end of the task, you will have one minute to tidy up your answers
So we've watched a lot of these videos.
Which ones stood out for you in terms of the funny story?
Well, I really liked the Liberty Sisters story.
Oh yeah What was that then?
Well, it’s a story about one of the band members Amanda.
Amanda’s got this reputation for sleeping in all the time.
Well, anyway, the band were meant to be playing at a local festival at Mayfu Civic Hall at 11 a .m.
on a Sunday Monday morning.
The other two met at 10 o 'clock at the MTR station and surprise surprise there’s no sign of Amanda.
So they get on the phone and she doesn’t answer.
Eventually after 20 minutes she answers.
She’s still in her bed.
Right, they say, we'll just go to the Civic Hall to set up and we will meet you there.
You would just have to arrive and go straight on, So Amanda agrees but she’s still half asleep and she gets it into her head the gig is at Chunwan Theatre and not Mayfu Civic Hall.
So she rushes to Chunwan Theatre and goes in the backstage door and somebody tells her she’s late and it started so she rushes on to the stage and suddenly realizes it’s the wrong show.
It's a show for kids with people on stage in costumes dressed as spiders and frogs.
So she just joins in and dances with everybody else, and nobody notices and she has a good time That's really funny, Was there one that you liked, Mitchell?
I really liked the story Selena Chung tells.
Oh. I didn’t watch that one.
Right, well, she was doing an audition for a show.
She’s the last performer on and she sings a really gentle ballad.
During the first verse she looks across and one of the judges is sleeping.
In the second verse two judges are sleeping and by the third verse all three have nodded off.
Oh no! Selena decides to keep going and reaches the end of her song.
The judges are still sleeping.
She goes over to the judges and sits down next to them and gently wakes them up and they are incredibly apologetic.
So they let her do another song and this time she decides to sing a real loud rock song to keep them awake.
She didn’t get the part for the show.
Oh well, they'll always be other shows!
I think that shows a pretty strong side to a character as well.
Yeah absolutely. I think my favourite was the Hilton College Band.
Did you listen to that one?
No, not yet.
No no. Right well, when they were 16 they were asked to play at the birthday party of a son of a famous Hong Kong actor.
They were playing at his house and there was a small stage built next to the swimming pool.
Their original singer was really good but he used to get really nervous.
In their first song he goes up to the microphone like a real rock star and the singer is so nervous that he's forgotten all the words.
So he’s you know, not trying to look stupid and still look cool so he very calmly walks to the back of the stage past the drums and promptly falls into the swimming pool.
Brilliant. Brilliant! It was then they decided they needed a new singer.
Brilliant! That is a fantastic story.
Yeah, Right, the other thing was I wanted to get some feedback from you, Mitchell.
Remember I asked you to take a look at the, let’s say, the unusual acts.
To see what they’re like, what have you got?
Well, there were a lot of, how can I put it, acts that maybe were not so suitable.
But one of the more exciting groups was The Cheerful Glee Club.
OK. Yeah, they're an acapella group.
An acapella group?
Yeah, an acapella group.
They sing songs and make music without any musical instruments you know, they just use their voices.
Just their voices?
Is this? Yeah.
OK, but that’s not that unusual is it?
Well no but they use their voices to create drum beats, violins.
and even animal sounds!
Oh wow! Exactly.
Exactly. It’s actually quite impressive.
OK, and any other groups that you’ve seen so far?
Yeah, there’s this all -girl Chinese orchestra group called The Flying Sticks.
Chinese orchestra? OK, so they use traditional Chinese musical instruments?
Yeah that’s right traditional Chinese instruments.
Well, what is so special about that?
Well, they are no ordinary Chinese orchestra group, They use traditional Chinese instruments.
to play pop songs!
Pop songs! Yeah, they play pop songs from, you know, like Lady Gaga, Katy Perry, performed in a Chinese orchestra style.
Nice. I'd like to hear that.
OK. Thanks Mitchell.
Actually I’ve got one last group I'd like to tell you about.
Oh, ok They're called the St.
St. Patrick’s Big Beats.
The St. Patrick's Big Beats?
Is St. Patrick's a school?
Yes, they are a marching band.
A marching band?
Yeah, you know, they play their instruments, you know, like drums and trumpets and they march at the same time.
Wow, so will they be marching up and down the stage?
They’re not sitting down at all?
No, so the special the special thing about them is that they march around in formation to form different shapes, Different shapes?
Yes, like shapes of stars.
Alright, marching and forming shapes of stars.
That I have to see.
